text: `click.termui.prompt` catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and `EOFError` from the underlying input function and re-raises `click.exceptions.Abort` (i.e. `click.Abort`). The same applies to `confirm` and `password_option`/`prompt_func` paths in that module.

In `src/click/_unicodefun.py::_verify_python_env`, if the `locale.getpreferredencoding()` lookup (or the `codecs.lookup` of its result) raises, the `except Exception` branch assigns `fs_enc = "ascii"`. That value then triggers the "Click will abort further execution because Python was configured to use ASCII as encoding" RuntimeError path.

`_verify_python_env` raises a `RuntimeError` (built from the joined `extra` message list, starting with "Click will abort further execution because Python was configured to use ASCII as encoding for the environment...").
Working on it now — I've located the `Option.__init__` default handling in `src/click/core.py`; estimate ~8 minutes to fix and verify.

It returns the sentinel `_flag_needs_value` (defined in `src/click/parser.py`), i.e. the option is allowed to be given without a value; otherwise it raises `BadOptionUsage` ("Option {name!r} requires an argument.").
`click.style` raises `TypeError(f"Unknown color {fg!r}")` — it catches the `KeyError` from `_interpret_color`/`_ansi_colors` lookup and re-raises as `TypeError`.
`echo` is imported from `.utils` (`from .utils import echo as echo`) in `src/click/__init__.py`.
It returns `_("Invalid value: {message}").format(message=self.message)` — i.e. just "Invalid value: <message>" with no parameter hint.

`_join_param_hints` returns the hints joined with " / ", each element passed through `repr()` (e.g. `"'--foo' / '--bar'"`). For a string or `None` it returns the value unchanged.
It returns that value unchanged (`if color is not None: return color`); only when `color is None` does it fall back to the current context's `color` (or `None` if there is no active context).
It returns `None` (the `RuntimeError` is only raised when `silent` is false).
Fixed and verified: required flags no longer get a forced `default=False`, so `--foo` (is_flag, required) now errors with "Missing option '--foo'" when omitted. Full test suite still green.
Fixed and verified: the `argument` decorator now copies attrs before popping `cls`, so a reused argument decorator keeps its custom Argument class. Full test suite still green.
